titulo.alumno:
«Запятая при причастном обороте»
Commas and participial phrases

intro: In writing, a long participle that follows the noun usually forms a descriptive aside set off by commas.

piezas.titulo: In writing, a long participle that follows the noun usually forms a descriptive aside set off by commas.
texto: In writing, a long participle that follows the noun usually forms a descriptive aside set off by commas.
If it precedes the noun, it is normally part of the noun phrase and is not separated in the same way: опубликованная вчера статья.

frases.estudio: Отчёт, подготовленный экспертами, содержит новые данные.
frases.alumno: The report, prepared by experts, contains new data.

frases.estudio: Подписанный вчера договор вступил в силу.
frases.alumno: The contract signed yesterday came into force.

pregunta.texto: Which phrase usually goes between commas when it follows the noun?

opciones.explicacion: The phrase appears after the noun отчёт and is set off with commas.
This form does not express the relation the question asks about.
Check which word governs the case or the structure.

pregunta.texto: What does this phrase mean? «Отчёт, подготовленный экспертами, содержит новые данные.»

frase.texto: Отчёт, подготовленный экспертами, содержит новые данные.

opciones.texto: The report, prepared by experts, contains new data.
opciones.explicacion: It corresponds to the first example.

opciones.texto: The contract signed yesterday came into force.
opciones.explicacion: That is the translation of the second example.

frase.texto: Подписанный вчера договор вступил в силу

piezas.traduccion: The contract signed yesterday came into force.
piezas.explicacion: Pay attention to the order of the words and to the grammatical form highlighted.
